input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper clears the shared statistics dict and gives the copy that same dict, so concurrent coroutines using the decorated function share and reset one statistics object.
- rationale: Trigger: two asyncio tasks, or a recursive coroutine, call the same decorated function while one is in flight. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() on the same dict and writes its attempt counts into it, instead of using a separate copy as before. Impact: statistics seen by an in-flight call are reset or mixed with another call's, giving silently wrong values.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. Every call shares one statistics dict and runs stats.clear() on it, so concurrent or nested calls, here async tasks or recursion, reset and mix each other's stats. Naming only the async path still covers the labeled failure path.
